title: Journey
statementMd:
There are $*n*$ cities and $*n* - 1$ roads in the Seven Kingdoms, each road connects two cities and we can reach any city from any other by the roads.

Theon and Yara Greyjoy are on a horse in the first city, they are starting traveling through the roads. But the weather is foggy, so they can’t see where the horse brings them. When the horse reaches a city (including the first one), it goes to one of the cities connected to the current city. But it is a strange horse, it only goes to cities in which they weren't before. In each such city, the horse goes with equal probabilities and it stops when there are no such cities.

Let the length of each road be $1$. The journey starts in the city $1$. What is the expected length (expected value of length) of their journey? You can read about expected (average) value by the link [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value).

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000$) — number of cities.

Then $*n* - 1$ lines follow. The $*i*$-th line of these lines contains two integers $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$) — the cities connected by the $*i*$-th road.

It is guaranteed that one can reach any city from any other by the roads.

## Output

Print a number — the expected length of their journey. The journey starts in the city $1$.

Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed $10^{ - 6}$.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is $*a*$, and the answer of the jury is $*b*$. The checker program will consider your answer correct, if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf9a7a80dafa0f6b2f4d2f115f2c4acade6b8b94.png).

## Note

In the first sample, their journey may end in cities $3$ or $4$ with equal probability. The distance to city $3$ is $1$ and to city $4$ is $2$, so the expected length is $1.5$.

In the second sample, their journey may end in city $4$ or $5$. The distance to the both cities is $2$, so the expected length is $2$.
statementZhMd:
七大王国中有 $*n*$ 座城市和 $*n* - 1$ 条道路，每条道路连接两座城市，并且从任意一座城市都可以通过道路到达其他任意城市。

席恩和雅拉·葛雷乔伊骑着马来到了第一座城市，他们开始沿着道路旅行。但是天气十分雾蒙蒙的，所以他们看不清马把他们带到了哪里。当马到达一座城市（包括第一座城市）时，它会前往与当前城市相连的某一座城市。但这是一匹奇怪的马：它只会前往他们之前没有到过的城市。在所有这样的城市中，马等概率地选择一座前往；当不存在这样的城市时，它就会停下。

设每条道路的长度均为 $1$。旅程从城市 $1$ 开始。他们的旅程长度的期望值是多少？你可以通过链接 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value) 了解期望值（平均值）。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000$），表示城市的数量。

接下来有 $*n* - 1$ 行。第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$），表示第 $*i*$ 条道路连接的两座城市。

保证从任意一座城市都可以通过道路到达其他任意城市。

## 输出格式

输出一个数，表示他们旅程长度的期望值。旅程从城市 $1$ 开始。

如果你的答案与标准答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 6}$，则会被判定为正确。

具体来说，设你的答案为 $*a*$，评测程序的答案为 $*b*$。如果 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf9a7a80dafa0f6b2f4d2f115f2c4acade6b8b94.png)，则校验程序会认为你的答案正确。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，他们的旅程以相同的概率在城市 $3$ 或城市 $4$ 结束。到城市 $3$ 的距离为 $1$，到城市 $4$ 的距离为 $2$，因此旅程长度的期望值为 $1.5$。

在第二个样例中，他们的旅程可能在城市 $4$ 或城市 $5$ 结束。到这两座城市的距离均为 $2$，因此旅程长度的期望值为 $2$。
